issues.legal_issue: Criminal proceedings may be quashed against accused persons when the complaint and investigation materials disclose no prima facie offence or participation by them, and their implication is intended to exert pressure in a civil dispute.
material_facts: The complainant alleged that, after buying disputed property, he was dispossessed and threatened. The complaint also alleged that a family member had forged property documents and rented the property to another accused.

The appellants were not parties to, witnesses to, or facilitators of the disputed sale transactions; the materials did not connect them with preparing the allegedly forged documents or delivering possession of the property.

The appellants were not parties to the civil proceedings concerning the property. The Court found that they had been implicated as family members to exert pressure to obtain possession and settle the pending civil dispute.
The appellants challenged the High Court’s refusal to quash the criminal proceedings against them.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should have quashed the criminal complaint and all consequential proceedings against the appellants. The appeals were allowed, and the proceedings were quashed as to them; the case against the other accused was left to proceed independently.
issues.legal_principle: Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure preserves the High Court’s inherent power to prevent abuse of the court’s process and secure the ends of justice. Under State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, illustrative grounds for quashing include allegations that do not prima facie constitute an offence or make out a case against an accused (categories 1 and 3), and proceedings manifestly attended by mala fides or instituted for an ulterior purpose (category 7). Vineet Kumar v. State of Uttar Pradesh, (2017) 13 SCC 369, relying on State of Karnataka v. L. Muniswamy, (1977) 2 SCC 699, explains that proceedings may be quashed where allowing them to continue would abuse the process of the court or undermine the ends of justice. The Court noted that these principles were followed in Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 315.

predicates.challenge_to_refusal_to_quash_criminal_p: The accused sought review of a decision refusing to terminate criminal proceedings against them.
predicates.complaint_does_not_connect_accused_to_of: The complaint and investigation materials did not connect the accused to the alleged criminal conduct underlying the disputed transaction or documents.
predicates.accused_had_no_role_in_property_transact: The accused were not parties to, witnesses to, or facilitators of the property transfer and were not shown to have prepared the disputed documents or delivered possession.
predicates.accused_implicated_to_pressure_resolutio: The accused were implicated as family members in order to exert pressure over possession of property and settlement of a pending civil dispute.

issues.definition: When accused persons challenge a refusal to quash criminal proceedings, the rule directs that the proceedings be quashed as to them if the complaint does not connect them to the offence, they had no role in the transaction or documents, and they were implicated to pressure resolution of a civil dispute.
